inclusion_policy: Primary peer-reviewed occurrence-rate studies with an Earth-analog, habitable-zone, or directly relevant FGK occurrence estimand, plus primary empirical Galactic-dynamics studies that directly test the source-to-target transport assumptions. Reviews are excluded.

primary_sources.definition: Table 5 Model 1 hab2 Poisson result with input uncertainties: 0.5--1.5 R_earth in the conservative habitable zone around 5300--6000 K stars
primary_sources.reported_result: 0.38 (-0.22,+0.50) planets per star for the constant-extrapolation low bound and 0.63 (-0.38,+0.94) for the zero-extrapolation high bound. The broader 4800--6300 K eta_Earth context is 0.37 and 0.60.
primary_sources.comparability: The 5300--6000 K temperature range matches v4, while Bryson's radius and full conservative-HZ domains remain much broader. The v4 posterior is reconstructed from this DR25 model, so agreement tests source fidelity rather than independent replication.

primary_sources.definition: 0.75--1.5 R_earth and 0.99--1.70 au around G stars
primary_sources.reported_result: 84.1% credible upper limit below 0.18 planets per star.
primary_sources.comparability: Broader radius range, semimajor-axis rather than instellation bounds, and a G-star host definition; not a like-for-like numerical test.

primary_sources.definition: planets within 20% of Earth's orbital period and radius around GK dwarfs
primary_sources.reported_result: Central estimate about 0.1 planets per star, with an allowed range from 0.01 to 2 after statistical and systematic uncertainty.
primary_sources.comparability: Conceptually close narrow Earth-analog box, but period replaces instellation, the catalog is Q1--Q16 rather than DR25, and the allowed range is strongly systematics-dominated.

primary_sources.quantity: eta_Earth under a stripped-core-aware occurrence model
primary_sources.definition: Extrapolation from a 0.5--6 R_earth, 2--400 day occurrence fit to Earth-size planets in the habitable zone
primary_sources.reported_result: Approximately 5--10% under the preferred interpretation; occurrence-model choices change the extrapolated value by factors of about 4--8.
primary_sources.comparability: Different catalog/model/domain and a broad HZ extrapolation. It is evidence that model form can dominate sparse long-period extrapolations, not a direct numerical validation of v4.

primary_sources.definition: normalized differential occurrence density near Earth for FGK stars, inferred from a 2--100 day occurrence model and extrapolated to longer periods
primary_sources.reported_result: Gamma_Earth = 15% (+6%,-4%) per natural-log period by natural-log radius area.
primary_sources.comparability: Gamma_Earth is a local density, not an integrated planets-per-star value for the v4 box. Converting it requires an explicit integration domain and model assumptions.

primary_sources.quantity: Kepler planet occurrence conditioned on stellar tangential velocity
primary_sources.definition: 0.5--20 R_earth planets over branch-specific period ranges around single FGK main-sequence Kepler stars grouped by Gaia tangential velocity
primary_sources.reported_result: High-velocity stars show lower 1--4 R_earth, P<100 day occurrence than low-velocity stars; the reported separation depends on the stellar-property correction and is about 1.55--2.55 sigma.
primary_sources.comparability: The result concerns close-in, much broader-radius planets and velocity groups rather than the v4 0.9--1.1 R_earth HZ target. It motivates a transport sensitivity but supplies no correction for v4.

primary_sources.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
primary_sources.quantity: Planet occurrence in thin-disc, thick-disc, and halo Kepler samples
primary_sources.definition: Kepler planets around chemically and kinematically classified Galactic populations, including 1--2 R_earth planets at 1--100 days
primary_sources.reported_result: Young, slow, metal-rich thin-disc stars have higher close-in super-Earth occurrence than the older thick-disc sample; the thick-disc and halo planet samples are small and stellar age, chemistry, and kinematics are correlated.
primary_sources.comparability: This is a direct Galactic-context occurrence comparison but not an HZ or narrow-instellation measurement. Its correlated covariates and sparse thick-disc sample prevent a transferable multiplicative factor.

primary_sources.quantity: Kepler DR25 occurrence as a function of isochrone and gyrochronology age
primary_sources.definition: 0.2--20 R_earth, 0.2--100 day planets around 1.5--8 Gyr FGK stars
primary_sources.reported_result: No statistically significant overall age trend; only a slight 1.5--2.5 sigma decrease appears for the low-mass, metal-rich stars dominating the sample, with conclusions limited by age precision and sample size.
primary_sources.comparability: The sample is contemporary and DR25-based but covers short periods and a very broad radius range. It cautions against assuming either a nonzero age correction or age invariance for the narrow HZ target.

primary_sources.quantity: Radial orbit migration in the low-alpha Milky Way disk
primary_sources.definition: Action-, age-, and chemistry-based dynamical model fitted to APOGEE red-clump stars with survey selection and measurement uncertainties
primary_sources.reported_result: Angular-momentum redistribution is much stronger than radial heating, so present-day Galactocentric radius can differ materially from stellar birth radius.
primary_sources.comparability: This is not an exoplanet occurrence estimate. It directly invalidates interpreting the present-day 7--9 kpc mask as a birth-environment selection unless migration is modeled.

comparison_findings: No listed literature value has the same radius, instellation, climate-intersection, host-temperature, and catalog definition as v4.

The Bryson et al. (2021) Table 5 G-star values of 0.38 and 0.63 are the temperature-matched source-fidelity benchmark for the reconstructed v4 broad-HZ medians of 0.388 and 0.659; this is not independent validation.
The v4 mean occurrence is numerically below broad-HZ literature estimates, as expected for its much narrower integrated phase-space box.
The absence of nominal DR25 candidates in the exact v4 box prevents a direct candidate-supported interpretation.
Published literature supports treating occurrence-model form and long-period extrapolation as material epistemic uncertainty not included in the v4 posterior interval.

Modern age and kinematic studies do not establish a transferable correction: Dai et al. (2021) and Bashi and Zucker (2022) report conditional close-in trends, whereas Sayeed et al. (2025) find no significant overall FGK age trend.
Frankel et al. (2020) show that radial migration mixes present-day radius and birth radius; the 7--9 kpc mask is therefore a present-day spatial estimand, not a birth-environment selection.
prohibited_inferences: Do not call literature values inconsistent with v4 solely because their point estimates differ.
Do not convert Gamma_Earth to an integrated eta value without specifying and applying an integration model.
Do not describe v4 as an independent reproduction of Bryson et al. (2021).
Do not treat the literature spread as a statistical confidence interval.
Do not convert close-in age or kinematic trends into an HZ correction factor without a matched occurrence model and selection function.
Do not interpret the present-day annulus as a sharply bounded stellar birth annulus.
